key_insight: A calibration-aware graph RL router can outperform gate-count-driven quantum circuit routing by deliberately choosing SWAP paths that avoid poorly calibrated couplers, improving final circuit fidelity.
engineering_relevance: For quantum compilers targeting noisy hardware, this suggests routing should incorporate up-to-date calibration data, not just minimize swap count or depth, to better preserve executable accuracy.
method: Trained a graph-based routing policy with proximal policy optimization (PPO).
Used same-day IBM Heron r2 calibration data to guide hardware-edge SWAP decisions.
Compared against SABRE-best20 and target-aware SABRE using exact simulated fidelity.
evidence_signal: Across nine MQT Bench circuits and three calibration snapshots, pooled mean exact fidelity was 0.727 for the learned router versus 0.440 for SABRE-best20 and 0.481 for target-aware SABRE.
watch_item: The fidelity gains come with more two-qubit gates, and the fixed tree action graph does not help all circuit sizes—10q families still favor SABRE-best20.
paper_title: Graph Reinforcement Learning for Calibration-Aware Quantum Circuit Routing
